gen_risks.description: Insufficient laboratory and surveillance capacity may limit detection and response to health emergencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Accelerate lab upgrades, procure equipment, train staff, establish regional lab network, monitor SLIPTA ratings.
gen_risks.evidence: Health systems … are fragile, with limited laboratory diagnostic capabilities and weak surveillance capacity.

gen_risks.description: Delays in recruiting required PIU staff and specialists could postpone implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set a recruitment tracker, use accelerated hiring, provide incentives, and have standby consultants for critical roles.
gen_risks.evidence: Legal covenants require recruitment of specialists within 1‑6 months after Effective Date.

gen_risks.description: Fiduciary risk due to substantial overall financial‑management residual risk.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update FM manuals, recruit external auditor, conduct quarterly internal audits, provide FM capacity‑building workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall FM residual risk is assessed as Substantial.

gen_risks.description: Procurement risk rated substantial because of possible delays, weak contract management and governance issues.
gen_risks.mitigation: Hire experienced procurement specialists, conduct early market engagement, use STEP for real‑time tracking, strengthen contract‑management training.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement risk is rated Substantial due to delays, governance issues, weak contract management.

gen_risks.description: Currency‑exchange fluctuations may affect budgeting as disbursements are in XAF while financing is USD.
gen_risks.mitigation: Open multi‑currency DA, include exchange‑rate buffer in budget, monitor FX movements, adjust disbursements as needed.
gen_risks.evidence: Designated Accounts will be opened in XAF for receipt of funds.

gen_risks.description: Conflict and fragility could disrupt field activities and delay the schedule.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pre‑position supplies, use CERC funds for rapid response, adopt remote training, develop contingency work plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility, Conflict and Violence lead to large displacements and may disrupt service delivery.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement may exclude vulnerable or disadvantaged groups.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement Umbrella Stakeholder Engagement Plan, conduct regular community consultations, strengthen GRM and gender‑sensitive outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks … relate to inadequate stakeholder engagement and exclusion of vulnerable groups.

gen_risks.description: Coordination challenges among multiple ministries and regional bodies could cause implementation inefficiencies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formalise RCC terms of reference, schedule monthly coordination meetings, share joint work plans, use a single project‑wide information system.
gen_risks.evidence: Implementation arrangements require coordination among multiple ministries; governance challenges identified as key risk.

gen_risks.description: Political instability in certain regions (e.g., Cameroon Northwest/South‑West) may halt service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Monitor political developments, maintain liaison with local authorities, design flexible activity schedules, earmark contingency funds.
gen_risks.evidence: Political instability, particularly in the North‑West and South‑West regions, may disrupt service delivery.

gen_risks.description: Civil‑works may generate waste, dust, emissions and occupational health hazards.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare site‑specific ESMPs, enforce waste‑management protocols, train workers on OHS, conduct regular environmental monitoring.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental risks are substantial and include waste, dust, emission, occupational health and safety.

gen_risks.description: Climate change could increase floods and disease outbreaks, stressing health infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient designs (green building, solar power), embed early‑warning climate data into surveillance, update NAPHS with climate scenarios.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change is a primary driver of health emergencies, increasing floods and disease outbreaks.

gen_risks.description: Large IDP flows and security challenges may threaten project implementation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct Security Risk Assessments, develop Security Management Plans, hire security specialists, coordinate with UN/NGO security units.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility, Conflict and Violence resulted in 1.1 million new IDPs in the region.

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with Environmental and Social Standards could trigger sanctions or project delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Ensure ESCP is fully operational, train staff on ESS requirements, perform periodic compliance audits, embed ESS checks in M&E.
gen_risks.evidence: Project prepared under ESF; ESS1,2,3,4,5,10 relevant; compliance essential.

gen_risks.description: Macroeconomic constraints and low domestic health funding may create financing gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Support domestic resource mobilisation (budget coding, medium‑term expenditure frameworks), align health‑security spending with national plans, seek additional donor pledges.
gen_risks.evidence: Macroeconomic outlook challenging; low domestic health funding; high reliance on external aid.

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
